query: What factors explain low review scores?

per_column.name: misleading_description
per_column.rationale: This captures a candidate cause of a low score -- the product description being misleading (undisclosed limitations, false claims, not as pictured). This is a plausible driver of dissatisfaction and thus functions as a treatment/candidate cause whose effect on the outcome is being attributed. It is not a common cause of any other treatment, so it does not serve as a confounder; it is itself a treatment.

per_column.name: ingredient_health_risk
per_column.rationale: This captures another candidate cause -- perceived health risks of ingredients (added sugar, allergens, additives) that could drive a reviewer to leave a low score. It is a parallel candidate cause, not a common cause of the other treatment and the outcome, so it is a treatment rather than a confounder.

judge.rationale: Both added columns are candidate causes (treatments) of the outcome, extracted from the review text -- they enumerate reasons a review might be negative. However, the technical claim requires BOTH a treatment AND confounders: variables that plausibly cause both a treatment and the outcome and must be adjusted for to avoid biased attribution. No such common-cause variable is supplied. There is no reviewer characteristic, product category, price, expectation level, or purchase context that would confound the treatment-outcome relationship. The two columns are essentially two candidate treatments with no adjustment set, so the causal estimation is not set up: attribution here would be an unadjusted comparison. The decisive confounder-surfacing test is therefore not satisfied (there are zero confounders to surface).
